parole.significato: The Islamic act of washing parts of the body using water for ritual prayers and for handling and reading the Qur'an.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish آبدست (modern Turkish abdest), from Classical Persian آبْدَسْت (ābdast), compound of آب (āb, “water”) and دست (dast, “hand”).

parole.significato: An honorific for high officials used in Turkey and certain Muslim countries.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish آغا (aghā, agha) (Turkish ağa ).

parole.significato: A silver coin minted during the Ottoman Empire, valued at one-third of a para.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish آقچه (akça, akçe) (compare Turkish akçe).

parole.significato: In a French, or (loosely) European style.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish آلافرانغه (alafranga), from Italian alla franca.

parole.significato: In a Turkish style.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish آلاتورقه (alaturka), from Italian alla turca.

parole.significato: A horse-drawn carriage once used for transportation in pre-modern Turkey.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish عربه (modern Turkish araba).

parole.significato: A high medieval Turkish feudal title, originally charged with the caretaking and mentoring of the realm's crown prince.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish آتابك (atabeg) (modern Turkish atabey), first used by the Seljuks, from آتا (ata, “father”) and بك (beg, “prince”).

parole.testo: From the city of Balaklava in Crimea, from Ottoman Turkish بالقلاوه (modern Turkish balıklava), alteration of بالقلاغه (balıklaga, “fishing ground”). During the Crimean War the British troops suffered from cold due to improper clothing. When the news spread in the home front after the Battle of Bala

parole.significato: Of or relating to the Balkan Peninsula.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish بالقان, modern Turkish balkan (“wooded, craggy mountain range”), from which the name of the region of Turkmenistan is derived, too.

parole.significato: An irregular soldier of the Ottoman army, reputed to be brutal and undisciplined.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish باشی بوزوق (başıbozuk, “civilian; irregular soldier”, literally “broken head”) (whence modern Turkish başıbozuk; possibly alluding to the soldiers being effectively leaderless, or to them acting “crazy”), from باشی (possessive of باش (baş, “head”)) + بوزوق (bozuk, “brok

parole.significato: A unit of weight established in 1931 equal to 10 kg.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish بطمان (batman). Cognate with Chagatai [script needed] (bātmān).

parole.significato: An indoor marketplace in the Ottoman Empire.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish بدستان (bedesten).

parole.significato: Wearing a fez (“a felt hat shaped like a truncated cone with a tassel attached”); fezzed.
parole.testo: From be- (prefix intensifying adjectives with the sense ‘adorned with something’) + fezzed (“wearing a fez”). parole.significato: Of or relating to Bektashism.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish بَكتاشی (Bektâşî).

parole.significato: A governor of a province or district in the Turkish (e.g. Ottoman) dominions.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish بك (bey, “gentleman, chief”), from Old Anatolian Turkish بك (beg, “ruler”), from Proto-Turkic *bēg (“lord”). See there for more.

parole.significato: The governor of a province of the Ottoman Empire, ranking immediately below the grand vizier. (Ottoman administrative t…
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish بكلر بكی (beyler beyi).

parole.significato: The jurisdiction or the territory of a bey.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish بكلك (beylik).

parole.significato: A major in the Turkish army.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish بیكباشی (binbaşı, literally “leader of a thousand”).

parole.significato: Nonsense.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish بوش (boş, “empty, unoccupied”). Entered popular usage in English from the novels of James Justinian Morier.

parole.significato: One of the imperial guards of the Ottoman Empire.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish بوستانجی (bostancı), from بوستان (bostân, “market garden”) (from Persian بوستان (bôstân)), and ـجی (-ci, “maker, dealer”).

parole.significato: Wheat grains that have been steamed, dried, and crushed; a staple of Middle Eastern cooking.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish بلغور (bulğur) (modern Turkish bulgur), by metathesis from older بورغول (burğul), from Arabic بُرْغُل (burḡul), from Persian برغول (barġul), پرغول (parġul).

parole.significato: A type of baked or fried filled pastry of the former Ottoman Empire.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish بورك (börek).

parole.significato: Synonym of kazasker.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish قاضی العسكر (kadilasker), see kazasker for more.

parole.significato: A large sheet-like wrapper worn over other garments in several Muslim cultures.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish چارشف.

parole.significato: A Turkish unit of weight equal to 200 kg (441 lbs.).
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish چكی (cheki).

parole.significato: A military decoration of the Ottoman Empire, a jewelled aigrette consisting of a central flower with leaves and buds, a…
parole.testo: Ottoman Turkish چـلنك

parole.significato: stews or rich soups found in national cuisines across the Middle East, Maghreb, Iran, Turkey, Southeast Europe, Central…
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish چوربا (çorba) and/or Classical Persian شورْبَا (šōrbā) or شورْبَاه (šōrbāh).

parole.significato: A member of a unit of irregular soldiers or resistance fighters; a partisan.
parole.testo: From various Balkan languages, all from Ottoman Turkish قومیتهجی (komitacı), from Ottoman Turkish قومیته (komita) from French comité (“committee”) + ـجی (-cı).

parole.significato: Synonym of Danishmendid.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish دانشمند (danişmend), from Classical Persian دَانِشْمَنْد (dānišmand).

parole.significato: A large Turkish double-headed drum, played with mallets.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish طاول (davul).

parole.significato: A Turkish outpost at a remote location, typically a mountain pass, manned by guards or villagers who receive tax relief…
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish دربند (derbend).

parole.significato: The guards charged with maintaining and defending a derbend in exchange for tax relief.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish دربندجی (derbendci).

parole.significato: An itinerant Sufi mystic practicing voluntary poverty in devotion to God, and often engaging in ecstatic rituals.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish درویش (derviş), from Persian درویش (darvêš, “poor; Sufi mystic”), from Middle Persian dlgwš (driyōš, “poor, needy”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *drigu-, cognate with Sanskrit ध्रिगु (dhrigu, “needy”) and Avestan 𐬛𐬭𐬌𐬔𐬎 (driguš).

parole.significato: Systematic collection of non-Muslim boys or young men from rural Christian populations of the Balkans, practiced by Ott…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish دیوشیرمه (devşirme, literally “collection, gathering”) (Turkish devşirme).

parole.significato: The commander of a castle or fortress in the Ottoman Empire.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish دزدار (dizdâr), from Classical Persian دزدار (dizdār).

parole.significato: An educated or well-respected man in an eastern Mediterranean or Arab country; often used as a title of respect or cour…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish افندی (efendi), from Greek αφέντη (afénti), vocative of αφέντης (aféntis), from Ancient Greek αὐθέντης (authéntēs, “lord, master”). Doublet of authentic.

parole.significato: A former administrative division or province of the Ottoman Empire.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish ایالت, borrowed from Arabic إِيَالَة (ʔiyāla).

parole.significato: A long coat, part of the traditional dress of Muslim women.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish فراجه (ferace).

parole.significato: A felt hat in the shape of a truncated cone, having a flat top with a tassel attached.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish فس (fes) (modern Turkish fes), named after Fez, Morocco, (capital of the Kingdom of Morocco until 1927), where the dye to color the hat was extracted from crimson berries.

parole.significato: a royal decree issued by a sovereign in certain historical Islamic states, especially by the Sultan of the Ottoman Empi…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish فرمان (fermân), from Classical Persian فرمان (farmān, “command, order, decree”).

parole.significato: A Turkish sailor.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish قالیونجی (“someone associated with galleon ships”) (modern Turkish kalyoncu).

parole.significato: A Muslim who has participated in a hajj.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish حاجی (hacı), from Classical Persian حَاجِی (hājī), from Arabic حَاجّ (ḥājj, “person who has performed the pilgrimage to Mecca”).

parole.significato: A communal bathhouse in Islamic countries and communities.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish حمام (hamam), from Arabic حَمَّام (ḥammām).

parole.significato: The private section of a Muslim household forbidden to male strangers.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish حرم (harem) (whence Turkish harem), from Arabic حَرَم (ḥaram, “something prohibited; sanctuary, women”); and later also from حَرِيم (ḥarīm) with same meaning, both from حَرُمَ (ḥaruma, “be forbidden or unlawful”). Doublet of haram and herem.

parole.significato: The chief consort of an Ottoman sultan; later, any of several consorts of the sultan.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish خاصكی (hasseki, haseki), from Classical Persian خاصگی (xāssagī, xāsagī).

parole.significato: In the Ottoman Empire, an edict countersigned by the sultan.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish خطِ شریف (hatt-ı şerif, “noble writing”), from Arabic خَطّ (ḵaṭṭ, “writing”) + شَرِيف (šarīf, “noble, sharif”).

parole.significato: A Muslim schoolmaster.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish خواجه (modern Turkish hoca), from Classical Persian خْوَاجَه (xwāja), ultimately from Sanskrit उपाध्याय (upādhyāya). Doublet of howadji, Khoja, Hoxha, and Osho.

parole.significato: A long-spouted pitcher, typically made of brass.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish ابریق (ibrik, ıbrık), borrowed from Arabic إِبْرِيق (ʔibrīq), possibly borrowed from Classical Syriac ܐܒܪܝܩܐ (ʾaḇrēqā), possibly borrowed from Middle Persian *ābrēk, or possibly borrowed from Parthian *ābrēk.

parole.significato: A boy servant recruited according to the devshirme system in the Ottoman Empire.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish (modern Turkish iç oğlanı).

parole.significato: An Ottoman soup kitchen built between the fourteenth and nineteenth centuries, often part of a larger complex or waqf.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish عمارت (ʼimaret), from Arabic عِمَارَة (ʕimāra).

parole.significato: A decree issued by a Muslim ruler.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish اراده, borrowed from Arabic إِرَادَة (ʔirāda), from أَرَادَ (ʔarāda).

parole.significato: A boy servant or page who was taken from Christian parents in the Balkans and converted, according to the devshirme sys…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish ایچ اوغلانی (iç oğlanı), from ایچ (iç, “interior”) + اوغلان (oğlan, “boy”).

parole.significato: The bodice of women or vest of men worn in the Ottoman Empire.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish یلك (yelek). Doublet of gilet.

parole.significato: A blunt javelin used by the people of the Levant, especially in mock fights.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish جرید (cirid) (Turkish cirit), from Arabic جَرِيد (jarīd).

parole.significato: A Turkish coffee-pot with a long handle.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish جزوه (Turkish cezve), from Arabic جَذْوَة (jaḏwa) or جِذْوَة (jiḏwa, “ember”).

parole.significato: Synonym of kazasker.
parole.testo: A reduced form of Ottoman Turkish قاضی العسكر (kadilasker), see kazasker for more.

parole.significato: The jurisdiction of a qadi.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish قاضیـلق.

parole.significato: A woman of a sultan's harem
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish قادین (kadın, “lady, matron, materfamilias; lady consort”).

parole.significato: A group of various traditional yellow cheeses from Turkey and the Balkans.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish قاشقوال (kaşkaval), from Sicilian cascavaḍḍu. Doublet of caciocavallo.

parole.significato: A very fine, vermicelli-like pastry used to make desserts in various Mediterranean and Middle Eastern cuisines, particu…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish قطائف (kadaif), from Arabic قَطَائِف (qaṭāʔif).

parole.significato: A Turkish armed policeman or courier
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish قواس (kavvas, “guard, sentry”), derived from Arabic قوّاس (qawwās, “archer”), from Arabic قَوْس (qaws, “bow”).

parole.significato: A lieutenant or deputy in various Turkish contexts, particularly
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish قایمقام (kaymakam), from Arabic مَقَام قَائِم (qāʔim maqām, “stand in”).

parole.significato: A subdistrict, particularly (historical) a third-level administrative division of the Ottoman Empire.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish قضا (kaza, “division of a sanjak”), from Arabic قَضَاء (qaḍāʔ, “jurisdiction, court circuit”), from قَضَى (qaḍā, “to decide, to judge”).

parole.significato: A chief judge in the Ottoman Empire. There were two kadiaskers: the Rumeli Kadiaskeri, who oversaw the European part of…
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish قاضیعسكر (kazasker), a reduced form of قاضی العسكر (kadilasker), from قاضی (kazı, kadı, “qadi”) and عسكر ('asker, “soldier”); compare قَاضِي العَسْكَر (qāḍī l-ʕaskar, “military judge”), from قَاضٍ (qāḍin, “judge”) + عَسْكَر (ʕaskar, “troops”). So called because the judge's juris

parole.significato: Fate; a predetermined or unavoidable destiny.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish قسمت (kısmet, “fate, destiny”) (Turkish kısmet), from Arabic قِسْمَة (qisma, “division, lot, destiny”).

parole.significato: A palace or other large official residence in Turkey or the Ottoman Empire.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish قوناق (konak, “mansion, station, inn”).

parole.significato: A coin of the Ottoman Empire, worth twenty piasters.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish مجیدیه (mecidiye), most likely through French medjidié, the adjectival form of the personal name Mecid, from Arabic مَجِيد (majīd, “glorious”)

parole.significato: A unit of currency of the Ottoman Empire in the late 19th century; used in Crete during the Russian occupation.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish متالك (metelik, metalik), from French métallique.

parole.significato: A semi-autonomous confessional community under the Ottoman Empire, especially a non-Muslim one.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish ملت (millet), from Arabic مِلَّة (milla).

parole.significato: A local official of the Ottoman Empire who oversaw a nahiye.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish مدیر (müdir, “local administrator, governor”), from Arabic مُدِير (mudīr, “directing one, governor, boss”), from أَدَارَ (ʔadāra, “to direct”).

parole.significato: A Muslim scholar and interpreter of sharia law, who can deliver a fatwa.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish مفتی (müfti), from Arabic مُفْتِي (muftī, “fatwa-deliverer”, literally “deliverer of formal opinion”).

parole.significato: A senior public official under the Ottoman Empire charged with tax collection.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish محصل (muhassıl), from Arabic مُحَصِّل (muḥaṣṣil).

parole.significato: The governor of a province in some Muslim contexts, particularly (historical) in the Ottoman Empire.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish متصرف (mutasarrıf, “governor of a sanjak”) (modern Turkish mutasarrıf), from Arabic مُتَصَرِّف (mutaṣarrif, “autonomous one, governor of a province”), from تَصَرَّفَ (taṣarrafa, “to act, to act independently”).

parole.significato: Synonym of sanjak: the territory of a mutasarrif.
parole.testo: From mutasarrif + -ate (forms nouns denoting rank or office, the concrete charge of it) as a calque of Ottoman Turkish mutasarriflik.

parole.significato: Synonym of salat (“Islamic prayer”).
parole.testo: Derived from Ottoman Turkish نماز (namâz) (Turkish namaz) and Urdu نماز (namāz), and their source, Classical Persian نماز (namāz).

parole.significato: An eye-shaped amulet supposed to protect against the evil eye in certain cultures.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish نظر (now Turkish nazar (boncuğu)), from Arabic نَظَر (naẓar).

parole.significato: The Turkish regular army; a soldier in the Turkish army.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish نظام (nızam), from Arabic نِظَام (niẓām, “order, arrangement”).

parole.significato: A room within a harem.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish اوطه (oda) (Turkish oda)

parole.significato: Synonym of Ottoman (“member of the Ottoman dynasty”).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish عثمان (osmân), from Arabic عُثْمَان (ʕuṯmān). Doublet of Uthman and Ottoman. Widely used as an anglicization of cognate names across the Islamic world, including Somali Cismaan, Persian عثمان (usmān /osmân), Malay Usman, and even Arabic عُثْمَان (ʕuṯmān) itself.

parole.significato: Synonym of Ottoman.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish عثمانلی (Osmanlı).

parole.significato: A ruler of a Muslim country or state.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish پادشاه (padişah), from Classical Persian پادِشاه (pādišāh) / پادْشاه (pādšāh).

parole.significato: A permanently entrenched wooden camp attached to Turkish frontier fortresses.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish پلانقه (palanka). Doublet of planch, plank, and phalanx.

parole.significato: The jurisdiction or the territory of a pasha.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish پاشالق (paşalık).

parole.significato: A highly seasoned, air-dried cured beef in Ottoman cuisine.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish باصدرمه (pastırma) (modern Turkish pastırma). Doublet of pastrama.

parole.significato: A sprite or supernatural being.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish پری (peri), from Persian پری (pari).

parole.significato: A dish made by browning grain, typically rice, in oil and then cooking it with a seasoned broth, to which meat and/or v…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish پلاو (modern Turkish pilav), from Classical Persian پلاو (pilāw), from Hindi पुलाव (pulāv)/Urdu پُلاؤ (pulāo), from Sauraseni Prakrit *𑀧𑀼𑀮𑀸𑀕 (*pulāga), from Sanskrit पुलाक (pulāka), which is probably of Dravidian origin. Akin to Tamil புழுக்கு (puḻukku, “cooked rice”).

parole.significato: Synonym of locoum.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish راحت لوقوم (rahat lokum), vulgar form of راحت الحلقوم (râhatü'l-hulkûm), from Arabic رَاحَة الْحُلْقُوم (rāḥat al-ḥulqūm).

parole.significato: A Turkish liqueur flavored with anise.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish راقی (rakı), from Arabic عَرَقِيّ (ʕaraqiyy, “of liquor”), from عَرَق (ʕaraq, “arrack, arak”), literally, “sweat”, “condensate,” which refers to an ouzo-like liqueur made of raisins. Doublet of rakija.

parole.significato: The holder of an Ottoman military rank akin to that of naval captain.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish رئیس, from Arabic رَئِيس (raʔīs, “head, chief, leader”)

parole.significato: A district, a prefecture, particularly (historical) a second-level administrative division of the Ottoman Empire.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish سنجاق (sancâk, “subdivision of a vilayet”, literally “flag, banner”), from Proto-Turkic *sančgak (“lance, streamer attached to a spear”).

parole.significato: Synonym of sanjak.
parole.testo: From sanjak (“sanjakbey, the governor of a sanjak”) + -ate, from Ottoman Turkish سنجاق (sancâk, “sanjak, banner”).

parole.significato: An official of the Ottoman Empire who oversaw a sanjak.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish سنجاقبكی (sancakbeyi), from سنجاق (“sanjak, banner”) + بك (“bey, ruler”) + ـی (“possessive”).

parole.significato: A dumpling of minced meat and other ingredients wrapped in a leaf (grape or cabbage).
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish صرمه (sarma).

parole.significato: A swindler.
parole.testo: From variant forms of Ottoman Turkish إسكندرون (İskenderūn) under influence from English -oon. Compare Stambul and Stamboul for Istanbul. In reference to the pigeons, supposedly derived from the use of the pigeon to carry messages from the English factory at Iskanderun to Aleppo upon the arrival of

parole.significato: Part of a Turkish palace or house kept for men.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish سلاملق or modern Turkish selamlık, from Arabic سَلَام (salām).

parole.significato: The swordbearer of a Turkish chief; a member of a Turkish cavalry corps.
parole.testo: Corrupt from Ottoman Turkish سلاحدار (silahdar, literally “weapon-bearer”), the first part being the Arabic سِلَاح (silāḥ, “weapon”) and the second the Persian ـدار (-dâr, “bearer”) suffix.

parole.significato: Of or related to Seljuk, to his dynasty, to their empire in southwestern Asia, or to the period of their rule from the…
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish سلجوق (selcuk), ultimately from Old Anatolian Turkish سلجك (sälcük) attested in the Dede Korkut and Karakhanid سلجك (Selcuk) attested in Mahmud al-Kashgari's Dīwān Lughāt al-Turk, of uncertain etymology. Compare modern Turkish Selçuk. Pelliot & al. favored derivation via Arabic

parole.significato: A commander in the Ottoman Empire.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish سرعسكر (serasker), from Persian سرعسکر (sar'askar), a compound word from Persian سر (sar, “head”) and Arabic عَسْكَر (ʕaskar, “army”), itself from Persian لشکر (laškar, “army”).

parole.significato: The holder of a particular military rank in the Ottoman Empire.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish سردار (serdâr), from Persian سردار (sardâr). Doublet of Sardar.

parole.significato: A fountain for ablutions, usually attached to a mosque.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish شادروان (şadırvan), from Classical Persian شَادُرْوَان (šādurwān), from Middle Persian šʾtʾwlwʾn' (/⁠šādurwān⁠/, “dais, platform; basin, pond, fountain”).

parole.significato: A dessert of frozen fruit juice with a dairy product such as milk added; a sorbet with dairy ingredients.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish شربت (şerbet), borrowed from Classical Persian شَرْبَت (šarbat), borrowed from Arabic شَرْبَة (šarba), from شَرِبَ (šariba). Doublet of sorbet and sharbat, related to syrup.

parole.significato: An Algerian cavalryman in the French army.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish سپاهی, from Classical Persian سپاهی (sipāhī), from Middle Persian spʿh / 𐭮𐭯𐭠𐭧 (spāh). Doublet of spahi and sepoy.

parole.significato: A religious student, especially in Turkey
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish صوفته (“theology student”) (modern Turkish softa), from Classical Persian سوخته (sōxta).

parole.significato: A mystic Muslim; a Muslim ascetic; a practitioner of Sufism.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish صوفی (sufi), from Arabic صُوفِيّ (ṣūfiyy, “man of wool”).

parole.significato: In Turkey, a dervish or Sufi lodge or place of worship; alternative form of takya.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish تكه (tekke), from Classical Persian تکیه (takya). Doublet of takya, takiyya, and takyeh.

parole.significato: Synonym of Karapapakh.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish تراكمه (Terâkime), plural of Ottoman Turkish تركمان (Türkmân).

parole.significato: A fiefdom in the Ottoman Empire granted by the Sultan to a spahi in exchange for his cavalryman service and cultivated…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish تیمار (timar), from Persian تیمار (timâr).

parole.significato: A Turkish musket
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish تفنك (tüfenk)

parole.significato: A small mausoleum built over the grave of a high-ranking or holy Muslim, especially under the Ottomans.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish تربه (türbe), from Arabic تُرْبَة (turba, “tomb”). Doublet of turbah.

parole.significato: Synonym of Turkmen.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish تركمان (Türkmân), from Persian ترکمان (torkamân). Doublet of Turcoman and Turkmen. As singular of Turkmen, influenced by the English man, plural men.

parole.significato: A province, particularly (historical) the first-level administrative divisions of the Ottoman Empire.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish ولایت (vilayet, “province”), from Arabic وِلَايَة (wilāya, “province, administration”). Doublet of wilaya, wilayat, and Blighty.

parole.significato: A high-ranking official or minister in an Islamic government, especially in the Ottoman Empire.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish وزیر (vezir) (Turkish vezir) (via French vizir), from Arabic وَزِير (wazīr, “helper, aide, minister”, literally “one who bears (the burden of office)”). Doublet of wazir.

parole.significato: A type of house, particularly found on the Bosporus.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish یالی (yalı), from Greek γιαλός (gialós).

parole.significato: A type of sword used in Muslim countries from the mid-16th to late 19th centuries.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish یتاغان (modern Turkish yatağan), related to Old Turkic [script needed] (yat-, “to bend, incline; to lie”), whence also words like yatmak (“to lie”), yatak (“bed”), yatay (“horizontal”), etc.

parole.significato: A milk-based product stiffened by a bacterium-aided curdling process, and sometimes mixed with fruit or other flavoring.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish یوغورت (yoğurt). Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *yogrut.

parole.significato: A thin, round, unleavened flatbread in Turkish cuisine.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish یوفقه (yufka).

parole.significato: A kind of Turkish rug from Konya and Karaman regions.
parole.testo: From the Yörük people, from Ottoman Turkish یوروك (yüruk, yörük, “active, fast; nomadic”).

parole.significato: An ornamental container designed to hold a coffee cup or teacup and insulate it from the hand of the drinker.
parole.testo: Likely borrowed from Ottoman Turkish ظَرْف (zarf), ultimately from Arabic ظَرْف (ẓarf). Also influenced by Classical Persian ظَرْف (zarf) and Hindustani (Hindi ज़र्फ़ (zarf) / Urdu ظَرْف (zarf)).

parole.significato: A Turkish dessert resembling rice pudding, coloured yellow with saffron.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish زرده (zerde, “zerde”), from Persian زرد (zard, “yellow”).

parole.significato: A form of land tenure in the Ottoman Empire.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish زعامت (zeamet), from Arabic زَعَامَة (zaʕāma, “leadership”)

parole.significato: One of a set of small finger cymbals used in belly dancing and similar performances.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish زل (zil).
